verdict.rationale: Windmill documents first-party triggers for scripts and flows, including emails, webhooks, HTTP routes, Postgres, and message brokers such as Kafka, NATS, SQS, MQTT, GCP and Azure Event Grid. That covers the email case directly and lets other apps push events through webhooks or infrastructure-level sources. However, the evidence never shows connected-app event triggers such as a new CRM record, a chat message, or a form submission; those would require each app to call a webhook. missing for 10: native connected-app event triggers (new record, chat message, form submission), documentation of per-app trigger setup for ops users, independent or hands-on corroboration of event triggering.

support.subject: As an ops user, I can trigger workflows from events in connected apps (new record, message, email, form submission)

citations.quote: Use schedules, webhooks, emails, HTTP routes, websockets, Kafka, Postgres, NATS, SQS, MQTT, GCP, Azure Event Grid and more.
Flows additionally expose version-pinned webhook endpoints
